children: Claude developer heads to public markets at a roughly $1.5 trillion fully diluted valuation.
🔔 Anthropic arrives with an $83 price tag
Anthropic is expected to begin trading on Nasdaq today under
after pricing its IPO at $83 a share. The company confirmed the terms Wednesday, exceeding its original $70–78 range as investors sought exposure to the business behind Claude.
The offering expanded to 980 million shares from the initially planned 825 million, putting its gross value at $81.3 billion, the biggest-ever IPO.
Anthropic is selling about 956.4 million shares, with existing shareholders selling the remainder. Most proceeds therefore go toward funding the company rather than cashing out investors.

Underwriters also have a 30-day option to buy another 147 million shares, potentially increasing the offering further. Today’s opening market price can differ substantially from the $83 allocation price, making the first trade a fresh valuation decision for investors buying through their brokerage accounts.

The IPO values Anthropic at roughly $1.1 trillion on outstanding shares, or $1.5 trillion including securities such as options and restricted stock. Reuters reported those figures alongside a separate $26 billion private placement.

Third-quarter revenue reached $16.96 billion, up 47% from the previous quarter. Annualized revenue run rate reached $81 billion by October 31, according to its filing. That run rate extrapolates the recent pace of business; it does not mean Anthropic has already booked $81 billion in annual revenue.
The spending requirements are equally substantial. Anthropic reported a $567 million quarterly operating loss and nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with infrastructure partners.
Those commitments extend into the future, leaving investors to assess whether growing customer demand can support the capacity being contracted.

title: ANT: Anthropic Prices $81 Billion IPO at $83, Sets Stage for Largest-Ever Trading Debut
